# A Trillion Dollars and a Firebomb: The Parallel Realities of the AI Era

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> documenting a single week in April 2026 in which AI companies' combined
> valuation exceeded a trillion dollars, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home was
> firebombed and shot at, a city councilman's home was hit by 13 bullets
> over a data center vote, and Snap laid off 1,000 employees citing AI.
> The book deliberately offers no prescriptions — it maps the structure
> connecting simultaneous capital concentration, labor displacement,
> social sentiment polarization, and institutional lag. As stated in the
> preface: "本書は、答えを出さない。しかし、構造が見えたとき、読者の中で
> 何かが変わる。" ("This book offers no answers. But once the structure is
> visible, something changes in the reader.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/a-trillion-and-a-firebomb_JP.md): まえがき・序章・全9章・終章収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/a-trillion-and-a-firebomb_EN.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book documents the same week in April 2026: a firebomb thrown at
  Sam Altman's SF home (Apr 10), a shooting at the same home two days
  later, 13 bullets fired into Indianapolis councilman Dan Gibson's home
  over a data-center vote with a note reading "NO DATA CENTERS," Snap
  cutting 1,000 jobs (16%) while citing "65%+ of new code generated by
  AI," and Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI-SpaceX combined valuations exceeding $2.7T
- The book cites Stanford HAI × Pew Research: AI experts vs. the general
  public differ by 52 points on whether AI will personally benefit them
  (76% vs. 24%), 39 points on societal benefit, and 35 points on trusting
  AI with major decisions
- The book cites Gallup's "Voice of Gen Z" study: 31% of Gen Z report
  anger toward AI versus 22% excitement and only 18% hope — anger
  exceeding hope by 13 points
- The book cites layoffs.fyi: ~80 US tech companies cut ~71,440 jobs in
  the first months of 2026, the fastest pace on record, with an increasing
  share explicitly citing AI (Klarna ~700 FTE-equivalent in support,
  Chegg -22%, Duolingo -10% contractors, IBM's 2023 plan to replace 7,800
  roles)
- The book applies Piketty's r>g framework to AI capital, citing Daron
  Acemoglu's NBER paper ("The Simple Macroeconomics of AI"): a projected
  -0.72% change in consumer welfare over 10 years, and Noah Smith's
  concept of a "permanent underclass" left behind by AI-driven capital
  returns far exceeding economic growth
- The book documents Anthropic's 7 co-founders pledging 80% of their
  personal wealth, and Dario Amodei's essay "The Adolescence of
  Technology" (Jan 2026) stating "the risk of tremendous inequality is
  very high" — alongside OpenAI's "Industrial Policy for the Intelligence
  Age" proposing a public wealth fund and robot tax
- The book presents Japan's distinct profile: lowest trust index among 28
  countries surveyed by Edelman (38), grievance score (65%) above the
  global average (61%) despite low AI adoption (15-25%, lowest among
  developed nations) and low perceived AI benefit (35%, per Ipsos) — a
  combination the book calls a "quiet crisis" with no domestic foundation
  model and near-absent AI regulation
- The book explicitly states it takes no position on whether AI
  companies' self-professed awareness of inequality is sincere or
  performative, presenting both sides as simultaneously true

AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of Leading.AI.
